S.FORM: Kekkeom.
S.TRANSL: A story.

S.FORM: Tuar qōn̄ nen, Wenagon mēlē vaten iasan vaten ra nutnutun.
S.TRANSL: Once upon a time, Wenagon was with his wife and his children.

S.FORM: Nir me sasa vavvan nen, nir tov van be dēdē n̄a.
S.TRANSL: They were living like that, until one day they went to gather canarium almonds.

S.FORM: Nēr me an sa, Wenagon tov dē.
S.TRANSL: So they walked up there, and Wenagon began to climb.

S.FORM: Wenagon me dē sa, ni ti vus ti u n̄a vavan, ma ni me tēr mēstēm tuar kariv n̄a ni tov so.
S.TRANSL: He climbed up the tree, knocking down bundles of almonds as he went up. Suddenly, as he tried to grab a branch, he missed, and fell.

S.FORM: Ni me so ror nen ma, ni tov mat.
S.TRANSL: He fell down on the ground, and died.

S.FORM: Ni me mat, nir tov le ni, sesen̄ ni a vere, gil mataqen nir tov tuvun ni.
S.TRANSL: When they realised he was dead, they lifted him up, carried him to the village, dug a grave and buried him.

S.FORM: Tuvun ni, a le qōn̄, ma ni tov tavraket a le mataqen nen,
S.TRANSL: But after they buried him that night, suddenly he rose again from his grave,

S.FORM: ni tov van abe vuvur nam-nēr, vus mamētē tuar wutve, tov sivtē ni ale mataqen nen sa nir me tuvun ni allon, wa –
S.TRANSL: he walked to their property, killed a pig, and threw it in the grave he had been buried in.

S.FORM: Sivtē ror wutve en allon, ni tov to den abe na-veran nen, ni tov to ti ale tuar vere. Ni tov sasa aben.
S.TRANSL: So he left the pig down in the grave, and walked away from his place – until he reached another village where he decided to stay.

S.FORM: Sa ti abe vere nen wa nir mēlē abe u tuar vere en, nir ve mōrōs te da tuar telvun̄.
S.TRANSL: One day, the people from that village, together with those of the other village, decided to organise a big celebration.

S.FORM: Ma nir tov da telvun̄ en, ni tov / tawa namun mēlē tov van ma.
S.TRANSL: So there was going to be a big party, where his wife was going to come.

S.FORM: Wa tawa namun en, ni te sa ti, ni te kere gor ti u wutve nen a le u mataqen; ni ve dōm si Wenagon nen wa – wa Wenagon ve to vata.
S.TRANSL: Meanwhile, his wife in her village had seen the pig in the grave, yet she thought it was Wenagon himself. She had no idea Wenagon had in fact gone.

S.FORM: Ni te kere gor ti u wutve en va–van, wutve en me dar, ni ve dōm si Wenagon wa, ni tov le qut wutve en, sun̄un ale get. Tov vatoko gor wev.
S.TRANSL: She kept an eye on the pig for a while, and once the body was decomposed, she took the pig’s skull – convinced it was Wenagon’s head. She put it in a basket, which she hung over her fireplace.

S.FORM: Vatoko gor wev tan̄ nen wa nir tov sasa vavan, din̄ ave u wasin̄in nen tabe nir ve-da telvun̄ aben nen, nir tov lak.
S.TRANSL: After she hung the basket like that, a few days went by, until that moment when people organised that celebration in the village, with dances.

S.FORM: Nir te lak ti a le qōn̄. Nir te lak ti a le qōn̄ ma tov nir te lak ti u mavto.
S.TRANSL: There were going to be dances at night – of those merry dances we called mavto, which villagers dance all night long.

S.FORM: Ma nir te lak ti, tawa namun en tov lak ma. Lak ran ma tan̄ nen, ma Wenagon mēlē tov lak ma.
S.TRANSL: As the dance fired up, the man’s wife joined in. She joined in the dance, and so did Wenagon!

S.FORM: Lak ma tan̄ nen, taem ruru ve rivrivtē ruru, Wenagon wa: “Qut wuruk ve sun̄un ale get!”
S.TRANSL: In the middle of the dance, when they stepped closer to each other, Wenagon exclaimed “It’s just a sow’s head in your basket!”

S.FORM: Ma nir tov lak mēlē.
S.TRANSL: And on they danced.

S.FORM: Lak mēlē va–van ma ni tov vit mēlē min tawa namun wa “Qut wuruk ve sun̄un ale get!”
S.TRANSL: They danced on and on, until he exclaimed again to his wife “It’s just a sow’s head in your basket!”

S.FORM: Tawa namun nen te ron̄ote gor ti.
S.TRANSL: The woman suddenly strained her ears.

S.FORM: Ni te ron̄ote gor ti, ale namun dōdōmi, ni wa “Sē wun te luwluw ti min na tan̄ ne? Mēstēm Wenagon wun e!”
S.TRANSL: She heard his call, and thought “Who could be talking to me like that? It sounds like my Wenagon!?”

S.FORM: Nir tov lak mēlē ma tan̄ ne, taem ni me vit ran mēlē si “Qut wuruk ve sun̄un ale get!”,
S.TRANSL: The dance started again and went on, until she heard once again “It’s just a sow’s head in your basket!”

S.FORM: ma tawa namun tov waw ran ameken; ma ni tov vit min ni wa “Wenagon, nik te karan̄ke ti!”
S.TRANSL: This time, the woman called back in reply; and then she added “Wenagon! You really are a crazy man!”

S.FORM: Ma kekeom en me bas aben ne wa.
S.TRANSL: And this is how my story ends.
